symbols.description: A boundary where plates move apart and new crust is created by magma pushing up from the mantle.
symbols.name: divergent boundary

symbols.description: A location or zone where plates move apart and new crust forms.
symbols.name: spreading center

symbols.description: Movement of tectonic plates, including movement of thousands of kilometers over millions of years.
symbols.name: plate movement

symbols.description: Molten material that rises from the mantle, pushes up to create new crust, and can squeeze through cracks or erupt.
symbols.name: magma

symbols.description: The Earth layer from which magma pushes upward.
symbols.name: mantle

symbols.description: Crust created at spreading centers by magma pushing up from the mantle.
symbols.name: new crust

symbols.description: Newly formed crust transported away from a ridge crest.
symbols.name: oceanic crust

symbols.description: Spreading process that transports newly formed oceanic crust away from a ridge crest and has caused the Atlantic Ocean to grow.
symbols.name: seafloor spreading

symbols.description: A submerged mountain range extending from the Arctic Ocean to beyond the southern tip of Africa and forming one segment of the global mid-ocean ridge system.
symbols.name: Mid-Atlantic Ridge

symbols.description: A system of mid-ocean ridges that encircles the Earth.
symbols.name: global mid-ocean ridge system

symbols.description: The rate at which spreading occurs along the Mid-Atlantic Ridge, averaging about 2.5 centimeters per year.
symbols.name: spreading rate

symbols.description: An ocean that grew from a tiny inlet between Europe, Africa, and the Americas through seafloor spreading.
symbols.name: Atlantic Ocean

symbols.description: A volcanic country that straddles the Mid-Atlantic Ridge and provides an exposed setting for studying spreading-ridge processes.
symbols.name: Iceland

symbols.description: A plate involved in the spreading center across Iceland that moves westward relative to Eurasia.
symbols.name: North American Plate

symbols.description: A plate relative to which North America moves westward across the spreading center in Iceland.
symbols.name: Eurasian Plate

symbols.description: Movement of one plate in relation to another, specifically North America moving westward relative to Eurasia.
symbols.name: relative plate motion

symbols.description: A volcano in northeastern Iceland around which consequences of plate movement are visible.
symbols.name: Krafla Volcano

symbols.description: A crack in the ground that can widen or newly appear around Krafla Volcano.
symbols.name: ground crack

symbols.description: The fissure zone along which numerous episodes of surface cracking took place from 1975 to 1984.
symbols.name: Krafla fissure zone

symbols.description: Surface cracking involving widening existing ground cracks and formation of new ones.
symbols.name: rifting

symbols.description: An episode of rifting along the Krafla fissure zone.
symbols.name: rifting event

symbols.description: Volcanic activity that accompanied some rifting events.
symbols.name: volcanic activity

symbols.description: Gradual rising of the ground by 1–2 meters before an abrupt drop and impending eruption during some events.
symbols.name: ground rise

symbols.description: Abrupt dropping of the ground following gradual ground rise during some events.
symbols.name: ground drop

symbols.description: Movement caused by rifting, totaling about 7 meters from 1975 to 1984.
symbols.name: displacement

symbols.description: Region where spreading processes have torn Saudi Arabia away from the rest of the African continent.
symbols.name: East Africa

symbols.description: Landmass described as having been torn away from the rest of the African continent by spreading processes.
symbols.name: Saudi Arabia

symbols.description: Continent from which Saudi Arabia was torn away by spreading processes.
symbols.name: African continent

symbols.description: Sea formed as spreading processes tore Saudi Arabia away from the rest of the African continent.
symbols.name: Red Sea

symbols.description: Actively splitting plate that meets the Arabian Plate at the triple junction near the Red Sea and Gulf of Aden.
symbols.name: African Plate

symbols.description: Plate that meets the actively splitting African Plate at the triple junction near the Red Sea and Gulf of Aden.
symbols.name: Arabian Plate

symbols.description: A junction where the actively splitting African Plate and Arabian Plate meet, at the meeting of the Red Sea and Gulf of Aden.
symbols.name: triple junction

symbols.description: Body of water whose meeting with the Red Sea marks the triple junction between the African and Arabian Plates.
symbols.name: Gulf of Aden

symbols.description: A zone under Africa where a new spreading center may be developing.
symbols.name: East African Rift Zone

symbols.description: Crust that can stretch beyond its limits, causing tension cracks to appear at Earth's surface.
symbols.name: continental crust

symbols.description: Stretching of continental crust beyond its limits.
symbols.name: crustal stretching

symbols.description: A crack that begins to appear on Earth's surface when continental crust stretches beyond its limits.
symbols.name: tension crack

symbols.description: An additional break in the crust produced by pressure from rising magma.
symbols.name: fracture

symbols.description: A volcanic landform that can form when magma erupts through widening cracks.
symbols.name: volcano

symbols.description: An event in which magma erupts, potentially forming volcanoes.
symbols.name: eruption

symbols.description: A zone ultimately produced by rising magma, pressure on the crust, and additional fractures.
symbols.name: rift zone

symbols.description: The planet encircled by the global mid-ocean ridge system.
symbols.name: Earth

symbols.description: Ocean marking the northern extent of the Mid-Atlantic Ridge.
symbols.name: Arctic Ocean

symbols.description: Continent bordering the Atlantic Ocean inlet described in the source.
symbols.name: Europe

symbols.description: Continental landmasses bordering the Atlantic Ocean inlet described in the source.
symbols.name: Americas

symbols.description: Pressure produced by rising magma that generates additional fractures in the crust.
symbols.name: pressure on the crust
